The respondent No.2 thus enhanced the compensation from Rs. 400/- per Sq. feet to Rs.1,225/- per sq. feet without according any reasons and has also awarded interest at the rate of 9% p.a., on the enhanced amount from the date of acquisition of lands till deposit of the compensation with the respondent No.3.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner has preferred this petition on the following grounds.
1) It is stated that the impugned Arbitral Award passed by the respondent No.2 is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of A & C Act.

2) The respondent No.1 approached the respondent No.2 seeking enhancement of compensation only on 12.12.2012 i.e., after a lapse of more than 3 years from the date of passing of award by respondent No.3.
A.P. No.7/2022 ought to have rejected the claims of the respondent No.1.

(3) If a request to refer the disputes to arbitration is filed beyond time, that is after a period of three years from the date on which the right to sue accrued, the arbitration has to reject the same as beyond the period of limitation.
(4) The respondent No. 2 without adjudicating the aspect of limitation could not have proceeded to award enhancement.

(5) The respondent No. 2 has placed reliance upon a letter dated 20.02.2019 issued by the respondent No. 3 wherein a request is made to compute the period of 3 years from the date of disbursement of compensation and on the basis of the said letter the respondent No. 2 has held that the compensation was disbursed during 2012 and the claim was filed in 2012 which is in time.

(8) The respondent No. 2 could not have relied upon a notification which came into effect after a lapse of 5 months from the date of publication of preliminary notification.

Explanation shows (1) that an award is in conflict with the pubic policy of India if the making of the award was induced or affected by fraud or corruption or was in violation of Section 75 or Section 81.
A.P. No.7/2022 (2) It is in conflict with contravention with the fundamental policy of Indian Law or iii) It is in conflict with most basic notion of morality or justice.

The petitioner has stated that the award was passed by the respondent No.3 on 10.04.2008 but the respondent No. 1 approached the respondent No. 2 seeking enhancement of compensation only on 12.12.2012 after lapse of more than 3 years from the date of passing of the award by the respondent No. 3.

It is stated that the respondent No. 2 ought to have rejected the claim of the respondent No. 1.

It is stated that A.P. No.7/2022 in this case right to sue accrued when the amount was determined by the respondent No. 3 under Section 3- G(1) of NH Act i.e., on 10.04.2008.

If the parties desire to proceed for arbitration they have to file an application for referring the dispute to arbitration in terms of Sub Section (5) which is within 3 years from the date when the amount is determined by the respondent No. 1.
If no such steps are taken the arbitrator has to reject the claim as barred by limitation.

In view of the above decision the application ought to have filed by the respondent No. 1 before 10th April 2011.
The application A.P. No.7/2022 is filed by the respondent No. 1 only on 12.12.2012.

On perusal of arbitral record, it is seen that the records do not contain the letter dated 20.02.2019.
The arbitrator without giving an opportunity to the parties could not have relied upon the letter to come to the conclusion that the application seeking for enhancement is in time.

In-spite of specific A.P. No.7/2022 ground taken by the petitioner that the application filed by the respondent No. 1 is barred by time, the respondent No. 1 has not stated the reason for the delay in filing the application.
.24. The respondent No.1 either before the arbitrator or before this Court has not stated why he has not received the compensation till 12.12.2012, even though the award was passed on 10.04.2008.
The respondent No. 1 has not explained the delay in filing the application.
The application filed by the respondent No. 1 before the arbitrator is beyond 3 years and so the proceedings before the arbitrator was barred by limitation.

.28. The Arbitrator has relied upon guidelines value dated 19.04.2007.
This document is not valid record received from the Arbitrator as none of the parties have produced and this is evident from the record of the Arbitrator.
Section 24(3) of the Act provides provision regarding hearing and written proceedings.

It reads thus:
"All statements, documents or other information supplied to, or applications made to the aribral tribunal by one A.P. No.7/2022 party shall be communicated to the other party, and any expert report or evidentiary document on which the arbital tribunal may rely in making its decision shall be communicated to the parties".
.29.

As an Arbitrator has relied on the estimated guidelines value of immovable properties and buildings dated 19.04.2007 without bringing to the knowledge of the parties and thereby has failed to follow the procedure under Section 24 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.
So the award has to be set aside on the ground of patent illegality.

.30. The petitioner has contended that the respondent No.2 has not assigned any reasons for re- determining the compensation nor he has assigned any reasons for enhancing the compensation or for relying upon notification dated 19.04.2007.

The acquired land is attached to highway.
It is prima facie suitable for commercial purpose.
No document is required for passing enhancement.

The payment voucher in-respect of Sy.No.
108/1 of Madavara village.

The above documents were not placed before the respondent No. 2.
So, same cannot be considered by this Court.
.35. The respondent No. 1 has relied upon the judgment in A.S. No. 82/2018 and A.S. No. 56/2018.
the said judgments pertain to acquisition in respect of Mulabagilu - Kolar, Bengaluru section.
The acquisition in the present case pertaining to Bengaluru North Taluka, whereas, the acquisition in t he above two judgments pertaining to Bengaluru East Taluka.
Apart from that the notification are different and the potentiality of land also differs.
So, the above judgments are not applicable to the case on hand.
